title: Org boundary leak caused by API key rotation window mismatch
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted + Dedicated customers in us-west + one Private on-prem deployment) reported intermittent '403: org mismatch' and session drops after API key rotations. Triage showed three related failure modes: 1) API key rotation TTL mismatch between the control plane and runtime agents causing stale API keys to be accepted briefly for the wrong org (org scoping leak), 2) a token refresh race in the runtime auth middleware that could return a fallback org when JWKS fetch failed during leader election, and 3) an edge case in Private deployments where admin-initiated KMS key rollover left a small window where old signatures validated but tenant-scoped claims were not reloaded. Impact: Several production requests were served under incorrect org context for ~30s windows during rotations resulting in billing attribution errors and one confirmed customer-visible data access alert (no exfiltration found).

Root cause (short): Inconsistent key rotation semantics across components. The control plane published rotation events with a 60s grace window; the hosted runtime cache applied a 30s cache TTL; dedicated runtime agent applied an optimistic refresh only on first request after rotation, which created a temporary mismatch. Additionally, the token refresh code in auth/middleware allowed an early-path return of cached parsed tokens when JWKS fetch was delayed, and that code path did not re-validate org claims when the signing kid changed.

Actions taken so far (hotfix & mitigation):
- Rolled out emergency config change to extend runtime agent JWKS cache to 90s to avoid asymmetric expiry (hosted roll underway; dedicated and private notified). (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4125)
- Deployed a patch to auth middleware to block-return if signing kid != cached_kid until full revalidation completes; this avoids fallback-to-default-org behavior. Patch landed to main and hot-fixed to runtime-1.21 branch for hosted. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4126)
- Sent targeted customer notices to affected tenants with incident summary and temporary mitigation steps. For Dedicated and Private customers, scheduled maintenance windows to upgrade agents and KMS policy ricochet.

Planned next steps (short-medium term):
- Complete canary rollout to us-west-hosted (3% traffic -> 25% -> 100%) and monitor org-scoped request counts and attribution. Metric dashboards: console.redwood.com/dashboards/auth-rotation-org-leak.
- Add strict assertion tests in integration harness: simulate staggered rotation windows and verify no cross-org acceptance. (tests added: tests/integration/auth_rotation_test.go)
- Align rotation windows and make rotation TTL an explicit contract between control plane, hosted runtime, and dedicated agents. Update protocol in confluence and add e2e verification in CI.
- For Private customers, provide a one-click migration checklist and a patch bundle for on-prem runtime-1.21. A follow-up release runtime-1.22 will include the full reconciler.

Post-incident follow-ups: incident postmortem doc, automated alert when JWKS-signed-kid changes with >0.1% of requests within 60s window, and a rollout of a 'rotation-sanity' test in the release gate.

References: Confluence runbook and PRs listed below. Forensics: request traces and sign-of-life logs stored in s3://redwood-incident/ENG-7932/.
